newsitem.title: USA: Photos of slain Colorado child obtained by tabloid.
newsitem.headline: Photos of slain Colorado child obtained by tabloid.

text.p: The murder investigation of six- year-old JonBenet Ramsey took a strange and embarassing turn for officials on Saturday when it was revealed a supermarket tabloid planned to publish autopsy photos of the beauty pageant winner.

Officials in Boulder, Colorado said an internal investigation was undertaken to determine how the photos were leaked to the Florida-based Globe and the family of the dead girl called the publication's editors "jackals, not journalists."
The office of Boulder County Sheriff George Epp released a statement saying it had undertaken an investigation of the theft of "official coroner's photographs by the Globe."
Three deputies assigned to the photo case were expected to work through the weekend and the office had "several leads," the sheriff's office said without elaboration.
Boulder city spokeswoman Leslie Aaholm said Coroner John Meyer, who learned Friday night the Globe had the photos, believed they were "authentic." One photo shows the murder weapon.
The planned publication of the photos left the family of the dead girl stunned and some local supermarkets said they would examine the tabloid before deciding to sell it.

"The ghoulish publication of these photos by the Globe is beneath contempt. It is a callous act and poses a grave threat to the integrity of the investigation of JonBenet's murder," Ramsey family spokesman Pat Korten said in a statement.

Autopsy photos are used as evidence in criminal trials. Police, who have kept quiet on most details of the murder investigation, have said they do not want to disclose aspects of the case that only the killer or killers would know.
The family asked other news outlets not to republish or televise the photographs. Epp's office said a private company, which it did not identify, processed photos for the coroner.

The Ramseys have also directed their attorneys to "pursue all available avenues of legal recourse," Korten's statement said. The sheriff's office said the person responsible for releasing the photographs "may face criminal and civil penalties."
A Denver radio talk show host Saturday suggested listeners ask their grocery store managers not to display the issue with the photos.
No suspects have been named in the Dec. 26 slaying of the little girl who was strangled and, according to published reports, sexually assaulted.
Her body was found by her father in the basement some eight hours after her mother said she found a ransom note on the backstairs on her way down to make coffee in the morning.

The leaking of the photos reflects the intense media attention that has befallen Boulder, a small college town about 30 miles (50 km) northwest of Denver. About 300 media represenatives have converged on the town.
The slaying has all the elements of a made-for-TV-movie: a ransom note, rich parents, and the child a contestant in beauty pageants.
John Ramsey is a prominent business executive and his wife Patricia a former Miss West Virginia.
